profiles.meeting_scenario: A postdoc in theoretical deep learning and a research engineer meet to troubleshoot why their internal reproduction of a paper on exploding and vanishing gradients in randomly initialized fully connected ReLU networks is not showing the expected exponential dependence on beta = sum_j 1/n_j. The context is a rebuttal-week replication check: the team has a notebook that should reproduce the paper's initialization-time Jacobian statistics, but recent runs show much flatter curves and inconsistent finite-width corrections. The agenda is to diagnose whether the discrepancy comes from the measurement code, the architecture sweep, or the initialization details, and to decide on a concrete rerun plan. The expected outcome is agreement on a narrowed root-cause hypothesis and a short set of reruns to validate it.

members.name: Dr. Anika Rao
members.expertise: Random neural networks, Jacobian analysis, finite-width corrections, theoretical deep learning
members.background: Anika has a math-heavy ML research background and helped write the lab's internal notes connecting edge-of-chaos intuition to rigorous Jacobian statistics in ReLU multilayer perceptrons.
members.private_state: She wants a reproduction that is faithful to the theorem-level quantity in the paper, because she worries that a looser implementation proxy could create a false negative right before an external presentation.
hidden_assumptions: "Gradient variance" in this project refers specifically to the empirical variance of the squares of individual input-output Jacobian entries, not a norm-based proxy.
"The paper setup" means the theorem-style synthetic experiment with equal-width hidden layers and zero biases unless someone explicitly says they are using an appendix variant.
"He initialization" here means i.i.d. Gaussian weights with exact variance 2/fan_in and zero biases, because that is the natural implementation of the theoretical initialization.
If beta is the control variable, then using architectures that isolate beta cleanly matters more than keeping parameter count or runtime approximately matched.

members.name: Evan Kim
members.expertise: PyTorch experimentation, efficient gradient logging, distributed sweeps, reproducibility infrastructure
members.background: Evan maintains the lab's experiment codebase and usually converts theory-facing desiderata into practical measurement pipelines that can run cheaply across many seeds and architectures.
members.private_state: He wants to stabilize the pipeline quickly without introducing a much slower exact-Jacobian computation, and he assumes small implementation details should not overturn the qualitative phenomenon.
hidden_assumptions: For debugging exploding or vanishing gradients, a minibatch-level proxy based on input-gradient norms is an acceptable operational stand-in for Jacobian-entry statistics.

"The paper setup" means the default reproduction notebook configuration already used in the lab, which was adapted from the appendix finite-width correction experiment rather than the simplest theorem sweep.
"He initialization" includes PyTorch's standard Kaiming initialization family, so Gaussian versus uniform draws and default bias initialization are secondary details.
If the curve shape across beta values looks qualitatively right after normalization, then the implementation is close enough to count as matching the theory for troubleshooting purposes.

misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a practical proxy: the variance of per-example input-gradient norms or related minibatch gradient magnitudes obtained by one backward pass.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML conversations about exploding and vanishing gradients, people often slide between exact Jacobian statistics and cheaper gradient proxies because both are described as 'gradient variance' and are expected to move in the same qualitative direction.

misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes exact i.i.d. Gaussian draws with variance 2/fan_in, zero biases, and fresh independent initialization per architecture-seed pair.
